instruments_location: Supplementary Table S9 (SMR results, GTEx whole blood and eQTLGen); not available locally: the local mmc1.docx holds figure and table legends only, no tables
notes: SMR with GTEx blood eQTL (main text says 'GTEx' blood dataset; version not restated for SMR; the paper's GTEx Dataset #5 is v7, n=369, and S-PrediXcan used GTEx v7 whole blood). SMR was run only on the 14 Sherlock-prioritised genes. Paper threshold: 'notable causality' = PSMR<0.05 and PHEIDI>0.05 (nominal, no multiple-testing correction); TOP3A meets it in GTEx blood (9 of 14 genes; 3 more suggestive with 0.05<PSMR<0.1). No SMR beta, OR, p-value, HEIDI p-value or top SNP is reported in the main text, and Table S9 could not be read, so estimate, p_value and direction are left empty; n_instruments=1 assumes the standard SMR top-cis-eQTL result. SMR results correlated between eQTLGen and GTEx (rho = 0.7, P = 0.0057; Fig. S5, not available). Outcome: overall EM in UK Biobank (Gene ATLAS; data-availability URL gives traits=503); controls not stated separately (total N 245,494). Title refers to ovarian EM, but that refers to the clinical samples; the GWAS outcome is endometriosis overall. Other evidence for TOP3A, not MR: Sherlock permuted P 0.0022/0.024/0.0028 (Datasets #3/#4/#5), MAGMA P 0.011, S-PrediXcan P 0.0032 (GTEx v7 whole blood; does not pass the paper's own Bonferroni threshold 4.46e-6), PBMC RNA-seq log2FC 0.56 (P 1.15E-08, 30 ovarian EM vs 30 controls), IHC higher in ectopic/eutopic endometrium, siRNA knockdown in EESCs. Headline: abstract and conclusion name MKNK1 and TOP3A as 'novel EM risk-related genes' / 'EM risk-associated genes, whose genetically modulated abnormal expression may contribute to EM' (read as a causal-gene claim; title also names them).

outcome_source: Rahmioglu 2023 European-ancestry endometriosis GWAS meta-analysis (International Endometriosis Genetics Consortium; GWAS Catalog GCST90205183)
source_location: Table S11 (mmc12.xlsx, Sheet1, row 4: probeID 2:11588931:11592776:clu_53175_NA, Gene GREB1)
instruments_location: Table S11 (mmc12.xlsx, Sheet1, row 4, probeID 2:11588931:11592776:clu_53175_NA): topSNP rs12470971, A1 A, A2 G, Freq 0.338187, b_eQTL/se_eQTL (sQTL effect) -0.749303/0.112321, b_GWAS/se_GWAS -0.0987/0.0088
notes: OR converted from SMR beta: OR = exp(b_SMR), CI = exp(b_SMR +/- 1.96*se_SMR); reported b_SMR 0.131722, se_SMR 0.0229739 (log-odds per SD of the intron excision ratio). Exposure: endometrial cis-sQTL (LeafCutter intron excision ratios + QTLtools, 206 European-ancestry women, 1 Mb cis window). Representative event = GREB1 intron with the lowest p_SMR: 2:11588931:11592776:clu_53175_NA, top SNP rs12470971; p_SMR_multi 9.833942e-9; p_HEIDI 0.5897582 (pass, nsnp_HEIDI 20); fdr 2.8557767568e-5; bf 5.7115535136e-5; p_GWAS 3.406678e-29, p_eQTL 2.538704e-11. Second significant GREB1 event (same cluster): 2:11588931:11591396:clu_53175_NA, top SNP rs72772088, b_SMR -0.124353, se 0.023334, p_SMR 9.860847e-8, p_HEIDI 0.2558866 (pass), fdr 1.9090599792e-4 (converted OR 0.8831, 0.8436-0.9244). The two GREB1 events have opposite signs, so direction refers only to the representative intron (per higher excision ratio of that intron), not to GREB1 expression; the text calls the two events 'a: exon 15 skipping' and 'b: intron excision' but the table does not say which intron is which. Significance: Results say 6 splicing events in 4 genes at FDR<0.05 (ARL14EP, GREB1, WASHC3, RP11-624M8.1), only GREB1 and WASHC3 passing HEIDI (p_HEIDI>0.05); Methods define significance as Psmr < 0.05/number of tested transcripts and PHEIDI >= 0.05; the table caption lists results at fdr<0.2. THISTLE-based sQTL SMR: no FDR-significant signal. Outcome: Methods/Results cite ref 17 (2023 European GWAS meta-analysis; key resources table GCST90205183), but the Discussion cites ref 41 (Sapkota 2017) for this integration; whether 23andMe data were included is not stated (the 23andMe data-use statement is tied to the Sapkota 2017 dataset in the key resources table); case/control counts not given in the paper. No colocalisation. Headline: abstract states GREB1 and WASHC3 were 'significantly associated with endometriosis risk through genetically regulated splicing events' (read as naming them as causal/risk genes).

notes: OR converted from SMR beta: OR = exp(b_SMR), CI = exp(b_SMR +/- 1.96*se_SMR); reported b_SMR -0.0933109, se_SMR 0.01962 (log-odds per SD of the intron excision ratio). Exposure: endometrial cis-sQTL (LeafCutter + QTLtools, 206 European-ancestry women). Only one WASHC3 event in Table S11: intron 12:102046119:102050189:clu_42350_NA, top SNP rs143511013 (in a non-coding exon of LINC02456, high LD r2=0.95 with GWAS index rs10860864 at the IGF1 locus); p_SMR_multi 1.975468e-6; p_HEIDI 0.6570071 (pass, nsnp_HEIDI 20); fdr 2.2947036288e-3; bf 1.1473518144e-2; p_GWAS 2.877677e-13; p_eQTL 3.636023e-10. Direction refers to higher excision of this intron (described as exon skipping in WASHC3), not to WASHC3 expression. The text is inconsistent about the exon (exon 6 skipping in Results/Discussion, 'exon 7 skipping' and 'exon 3 skipping' elsewhere). Significance: 6 events in 4 genes at FDR<0.05; only GREB1 and WASHC3 pass HEIDI; Methods threshold Psmr < 0.05/number tested and PHEIDI >= 0.05. Outcome: Methods/Results cite the 2023 European meta-analysis (ref 17; GCST90205183) but the Discussion cites ref 41 (Sapkota 2017); 23andMe inclusion not stated; case/control counts not given. No colocalisation. Discussion mentions a prior MR linking WASHC3 plasma protein to endometriosis (ref 63). Headline: abstract names GREB1 and WASHC3 as significantly associated with endometriosis risk through genetically regulated splicing.

outcome_source: Not stated: 'overall endometriosis' GWAS (subtype outcomes labelled endometriosis-fallopian and endometriosis-intestine, names that resemble FinnGen N14 endpoints, but the outcome dataset is never named)
source_location: Results section 3.7 (main text); Figure 7A, E, I; Table 1 (sensitivity)
instruments_location: Not reported as a table; the 18 SNPs appear only in Figure 7 (funnel, leave-one-out and scatter plots for MET)
notes: Two-sample MR, exposure 'pQTL summary data retrieved from the FinnGen database' (dataset, platform, tissue and sample size not specified). Instruments: SNPs at P < 5e-6, LD pruning r2 < 0.001 and 10,000 kb distance; no cis restriction stated, hence genome_wide. Only the 6 machine-learning core genes (PLAT, SELL, AXL, ESR1, MET, PIK3R1) were tested; MET and SELL nominally significant; the paper states no multiple-testing correction was applied. Subtype results: fallopian tube-type OR 0.673 (0.453-0.999), p = 0.0495; intestinal-type OR 0.727 (0.557-0.950), p = 0.0197. Sensitivity (Table 1, overall endometriosis): Cochran's Q 38.709, p-value 0.096 (note: Q = 38.709 on 17 df would give p of about 0.002, so the printed Q p-value looks inconsistent); MR-Egger intercept 0.020 (se 0.011, p 0.076); MR-PRESSO RSSobs 66.203, p 0.350; mean F 115.579 (min 31.336, max 1,034.491). Colocalisation not performed (stated as a limitation). MET mRNA down-regulated in endometriosis tissue (GEO arrays). Headline: abstract and conclusion name MET and SELL as key/core hub genes and core targets with MET showing a potentially protective association; Discussion says they 'may serve as potential therapeutic targets'.
